_comment: AUTHORED OWNERSHIP DECISIONS for CPC50220. Every family in families/ACI-CPC50220.families.json appears exactly once below.
_deliveredNote: 27 units across 10 clusters over 104 weeks. Cluster 1 WHS and risk, 2 legal and contractual, 3 building codes, 4 estimating and procurement, 5 site operations, 6 structural and technical, 7 surveying, 8 environmental, 9 quality and stakeholders, 10 financial. Ownership follows cluster order. Eleven units are shared with CPC40120; the two courses keep separate registers because the neighbouring units differ and so does what each unit must carry.

topics.name: The risk management process
topics.rationale: Cluster 1 is delivered first and holds both risk units. Identify, analyse, evaluate, treat and monitor is one method whether the risk is a fall from height or an insolvent subcontractor. BSBWHS513 is listed first in the cluster.
topics.teachingRule: BSBOPS504 Manage business risk applies the same five steps to commercial risk and teaches what is different - risk appetite, insurance, and the financial consequence of a treatment - not the method.

topics.name: Building and construction contracts and the obligations they create
topics.rationale: Nineteen of the twenty-seven units assume a contract sits behind the work. CPCCBC4009 Apply legal requirements sits in Cluster 2 and explains the contract as a source of obligation. CPCCBC4003 Select, prepare and administer a construction contract owns the mechanics of choosing and administering one; that content overlapped with nothing and is taught there in full.
topics.teachingRule: Estimating, site and technical units name the contract term bearing on their own output - a provisional sum, a variation clause, a practical completion date - and cite this topic rather than re-explaining contract law.

topics.name: Work health and safety duties on building and construction projects
topics.rationale: Seven units carry WHS duties as a legal obligation of the builder. Cluster 1 owns the RISK METHOD; CPCCBC4009 in Cluster 2 owns the DUTY - who holds it, to whom, and what breaching it costs.
topics.teachingRule: Site and technical units name the duty their activity triggers and the control that discharges it. Neither the method nor the legislation is restated.

topics.name: Builder registration and licensing
topics.rationale: Who may lawfully contract to build, and in what class of work, is stated once in Cluster 2.
topics.teachingRule: CPCCBC5007 cites the licence class and teaches the obligations attaching to holding it.

topics.name: Organisational policies and procedures governing project work
topics.rationale: Five units require work done in accordance with internal policy. Cluster 2 is the earliest cluster containing any of them.
topics.teachingRule: Later units name the policy governing their own output and do not re-teach what a policy is.

topics.name: Australian Consumer Law as it applies to building work
topics.rationale: Statutory warranties, misleading conduct and consumer guarantees are one body of law, owned in Cluster 2 where the contractor's legal obligations are the subject.
topics.teachingRule: CPCCBC5019 cites the ACL where it bears on deposits, progress claims and refunds.

topics.name: Business licensing and the Australian Business Licence and Information Service
topics.rationale: Finding which licences, permits and registrations a job requires is one research task, taught where the contractor's obligations are taught.
topics.teachingRule: CPCCBC5010 confirms approvals are in place before work starts and does not re-teach how to find them.

topics.name: Return to work and rehabilitation obligations
topics.rationale: Workers compensation, injury management and the return-to-work duty are a single statutory scheme, owned with the contractor's other legal obligations.
topics.teachingRule: CPCCBC5010 applies it to an injured worker on a live site and cites the scheme.

topics.name: Construction drawings and specifications as the project record
topics.rationale: Ten units extract information from the same drawing set. CPCCBC4003 in Cluster 2 is the earliest of them, and a contract is administered against the drawings and specification it incorporates.
topics.teachingRule: Estimating, codes and technical units take what they need and state which document governs where two disagree. CPCCBC4012 owns the reading skill itself in Cluster 6.

topics.name: The National Construction Code: structure, building classes and types of construction
topics.rationale: Cluster 3 is the codes cluster and is sequenced ahead of everything depending on it. Classification is the Code's first question, and CPCCBC4001 covers Class 1 and 10.
topics.teachingRule: CPCCBC4053 teaches the delta to Class 2 to 9 Type C and CPCCBC5001 the delta to Type B. Neither re-teaches the Code's structure. CPCSUS5001 and CPCCBC5010 cite the Code rather than describing it.

topics.name: Building defects: causes, implications and remedial work
topics.rationale: Defects caused by failure to apply codes, and the remedial work they demand, are one subject and are the reason the codes cluster exists.
topics.teachingRule: CPCCBC4053, CPCCBC5001 and CPCCBC4010 cite defects specific to their own scope and do not restate the taxonomy.

topics.name: Material properties, limitations and evidence of suitability
topics.rationale: What a material can do and the certification proving it may lawfully be used are one topic, needed the moment the Code is applied.
topics.teachingRule: CPCCBC5010 and CPCSUS5001 select materials against this knowledge and are assessed on the selection, not on the properties.

topics.name: Performance Solutions and Assessment Methods under the NCC
topics.rationale: Deemed-to-Satisfy against Performance Solution is explained once, with the Code.
topics.teachingRule: CPCCBC4053 identifies where a Performance Solution is likely and cites the method.

topics.name: Building design principles and structural behaviour under load
topics.rationale: Stress, strain, compression and bending appear in the codes units as the reasoning behind a provision, and Cluster 3 precedes Cluster 6.
topics.teachingRule: CPCCBC5018 extends this to multi-storey load paths and member sizing, which is genuinely new.

topics.name: Quality systems and best-practice approaches
topics.rationale: Compliance and quality are checked the same way, so they are taught together in the codes cluster.
topics.teachingRule: BSBPMG532 in Cluster 9 builds the quality plan, which is new content, and cites this topic for the underlying idea.

topics.name: Environmental requirements and sustainability principles
topics.rationale: The Code's environmental and energy provisions are introduced with the Code in Cluster 3.
topics.teachingRule: CPCSUS5001 in Cluster 8 writes the sustainability policy, which is its own work, and cites this topic for the regulatory frame.

topics.name: Below-ground construction methods
topics.rationale: Footings, basements, retention and waterproofing below ground appear in CPCCBC4053 in Cluster 3, ahead of CPCCBC5018 in Cluster 6.
topics.teachingRule: CPCCBC5018 applies structural analysis to below-ground elements and cites the construction methods.

topics.name: Workplace procedures, safety and environmental requirements on estimating and technical work
topics.rationale: Five units close with the same requirement that work follow workplace procedure and meet safety and environmental obligations. Cluster 4 is the earliest cluster holding any of them.
topics.teachingRule: Cluster 6 units state the requirement as a constraint on their own deliverable and do not restate it.

topics.name: Environment Protection Authority regulation of building work
topics.rationale: EPA licensing, noise, dust, run-off and waste tracking are one regulatory regime, met first in Cluster 4 where an estimate must price compliance.
topics.teachingRule: CPCCBC5013 reports against the regime and cites it.

topics.name: Temporary site facilities, storage and boundary fencing
topics.rationale: Site establishment is priced in Cluster 4 before it is supervised in Cluster 5. CPCCBC4005 must schedule and cost it.
topics.teachingRule: CPCCBC5003 plans the site layout and sequencing of those facilities, which is new, and cites the schedule.

topics.name: Temporary site services and permanent utilities
topics.rationale: Power, water, sewer and telecommunications - temporary during construction and permanent on completion - are one topic, and CPCCBC5002 in Cluster 4 must cost both.
topics.teachingRule: CPCCBC5010 coordinates the changeover on site and cites the costing.

topics.name: Digital documentation: computer-aided design and building information modelling
topics.rationale: CAD drawings and BIM models are two forms of the same digital documentation. CPCCBC4013 Prepare and evaluate tender documentation, in Cluster 4, is the earliest unit to depend on them.
topics.teachingRule: CPCCBC4012 reads them and CPCCBC4014 produces sketches from them. Neither re-teaches what a model is.

topics.name: Site communication: written reports, email and face-to-face
topics.rationale: Three families - written reports and memoranda, face-to-face verbal communication, and email - are one topic: choosing the channel that suits the message and leaving a record. CPCCBC4008 Supervise site communication and administration is the unit whose subject it is, and it opens Cluster 5.
topics.teachingRule: CPCCBC5010 uses the channels to direct work and is assessed on the direction being clear and recorded, not on knowing what a memorandum is.

topics.name: Human resource principles and practices on a construction project
topics.rationale: CPCCBC5003 Supervise the planning of onsite work in Cluster 5 must resource the job with people before Cluster 6 reports on their performance.
topics.teachingRule: CPCCBC5013 reports on human resource matters and cites the principles.

topics.name: The hierarchy of control applied on site
topics.rationale: Elimination through to PPE is the control logic BSBWHS513 establishes in Cluster 1; the two units in this family apply it on a live site, and CPCCBC5010 in Cluster 5 is the earlier of them. Recorded as its own topic because the on-site application - who selects the control, who verifies it, what happens when a higher-order control is refused - is not what Cluster 1 teaches.
topics.teachingRule: CPCSUS5001 cites the hierarchy when writing sustainability controls and does not re-derive it.

topics.name: Building and construction methods and terminology
topics.rationale: The vocabulary is needed first where drawings are read, in Cluster 6.
topics.teachingRule: CPCCBC4014 uses the terminology and is not assessed on defining it.

topics.name: Contour site plans and reading site levels
topics.rationale: CPCCBC4010 is listed first in Cluster 6 and needs the ground profile before it can reason about footings.
topics.teachingRule: CPCCBC4012 reads the contour plan as one drawing among the set. CPCCBC4018 in Cluster 7 generates levels, which is its own content.
